requirements.text: All vehicles shall comply with the provisions set out in Annex 3 to this Regulation.

Wherever there is a requirement for a surface in the vehicle to be horizontal or at a specific angle when the vehicle is at its mass in running order, in the case of a vehicle with mechanical suspension the requirement shall be met when the vehicle is in the loading condition declared by the manufacturer if the surface exceeds or possesses a slope at mass in running order.
The vehicles shall comply with the requirements of Annex 11.
The vehicle shall have a number (P) of seating places, other than folding seats, which conform to the requirements of paragraph 7.7.8. below.
Space shall be provided in the driver’s area, in a position clearly visible to the driver in his seating position, for the markings provided for in paragraph 3.3. of Annex 11.

If the engine compartment of a vehicle is located to the rear of the driver's compartment, it shall not be possible to start the engine from the driver's position when the main engine access panel located in the rear face of the vehicle is open and provides direct access to parts that represent a hazard when the engine is running (e.g. pulley of belt drives).

The stability of a vehicle shall be such that the point at which overturning occurs would not be passed if the surface on which the vehicle stands were tilted to both sides in turn to an angle of 28 degrees from the horizontal.
During the stability test, no parts of the vehicle which are not intended to come into contact in normal use shall come into contact.
During the stability test, no part of the vehicle shall become damaged or deranged.

No flammable sound-proofing material or material liable to become impregnated with fuel, lubricant or other combustible material shall be used in the engine compartment unless the material is covered by an impermeable sheet.

Precautions shall be taken, either by a suitable layout of the engine compartment or by the provision of drainage orifices, to avoid, so far as possible, the accumulation of fuel, lubricating oil or any other combustible material in any part of the engine compartment.

A partition of heat-resisting material shall be fitted between the engine compartment or any other source of heat (such as a retarder, or a device for heating the interior of the body other than a device functioning by warm water circulation) and the rest of the vehicle.
All fixings, clips, gaskets, etc., used in conjunction with the partition between the engine compartment or other source of heat and the rest of the vehicle shall be fire resistant.

In the case of vehicles having an internal combustion engine or a combustion heater located to the rear of the driver's compartment, the compartment shall be equipped with an alarm system providing the driver with both an acoustic and a visual signal, and activating the hazard warning signal, in the event of excess temperature in the engine compartment and in each compartment where a combustion heater is located.
All cables shall be well insulated.
All cables and electrical equipment shall be able to withstand the temperature and humidity conditions to which they are exposed.

In the engine compartment, particular attention shall be paid to the suitability of cables and electrical equipment to withstand the environmental temperature and the effects of all likely contaminants.
No cable used in an electrical circuit shall carry a current in excess of that acceptable for such a cable in the light of its mode of installation and the maximum ambient temperature.

Every electrical circuit feeding an item of equipment other than the starter, the ignition circuit (positive ignition), the glow-plugs, the engine-stopping device, the charging circuit and the battery earth connection shall include a fuse or a circuit breaker.
Where circuits feeding other equipments are protected by a common fuse or a common circuit-breaker, their sum rated capacity shall not exceed the capacity of the fuse or of the circuit-breaker.
All cables shall be well protected and shall be held securely in position in such a way that they cannot be damaged by cutting, abrasion or chafing.

Where the voltage exceeds 100 V RMS (Root Mean Square) in one or more electrical circuits in a vehicle, a manually-operated isolating switch capable of disconnecting all such circuits from the main electrical supply shall be connected in each pole of that supply which is not electrically connected to earth, and shall be located inside the vehicle in a position readily accessible to the driver, provided that no such isolating switch shall be capable of disconnecting any electrical circuit supplying the mandatory external vehicle lights. This paragraph does not apply to high tension ignition circuits nor to self-contained circuits within a unit of equipment in the vehicle.

All electrical cables shall be so located that no part can make contact with any fuel line or any part of the exhaust system, or be subjected to excessive heat, unless suitable special insulation and protection is provided, as for example to a solenoid-operated exhaust valve.
All batteries shall be well secured.
The battery compartment shall be separated from the passenger compartment and driver’s compartment.
The battery compartment shall be ventilated to outside air.
The battery terminals shall be protected against the risk of short circuit.
Space shall be provided for the fitting of one or more fire extinguishers, one being near the driver’s seat.
In vehicles of Class I, II or III the space for each required extinguisher shall be not less than 15 dm³.
Space shall be provided for the fitting of one or more first-aid kits.
The space provided for first-aid kits shall be not less than 7 dm³.
The minimum dimension of the space provided for first-aid kits shall not be less than 80 mm.
Where fire extinguishers and first aid kits are secured against theft or vandalism (e.g. in an internal locker or behind breakable glass), the locations of these items shall be clearly marked.
Where fire extinguishers and first aid kits are secured against theft or vandalism, means shall be provided for persons to extract them easily in an emergency.

No flammable material shall be permitted within 100 mm of the exhaust system component, any high voltage electrical equipment or any other significant source of heat unless the material is effectively shielded.
Where necessary, shielding shall be provided to prevent grease or other flammable materials coming into contact with exhaust system or other significant heat sources.

In the case of vehicles of Classes I, II, III and B, having the engine located to the rear of the driver’s compartment, in the event of activation of an alarm system, the emergency lighting system according to paragraph 7.8.3., if fitted, shall automatically activate.

In the case of vehicles of Classes I, II, III and B, having the engine located to the rear of the driver’s compartment, in the event of activation of an alarm system, after a single positive action of the driver on any of the door controls in the driver’s compartment, all power-operated doors situated on the side of the vehicle nearer to the side of the road corresponding to the direction of traffic for which the vehicle is designed shall open and shall remain in the opened position, when the vehicle is stationary or driving at a speed less than or equal to 3 km/h.

In the event of activation of an alarm system, a repeated use of the opening control shall not reverse the opening movement of the door, in order to avoid unintended re-closing in an emergency situation.
The minimum number of doors in a vehicle shall be two, either two service doors or one service door and one emergency door.
For a vehicle of Classes III & B carrying 46 - 70 passengers, the minimum number of service doors shall be 1.

For the purpose of this requirement, service doors equipped with a power-operated control system shall not be deemed to be emergency doors unless they can be readily opened by hand, once the control prescribed in paragraph 7.6.5.1. below has been actuated, if necessary.
The minimum number of emergency exits shall be such that the total number of exits in a separate compartment is as given in the table of paragraph 7.6.1.4.
The number of exits for each separate deck (in the case of a double-deck vehicle) and each separate compartment shall be determined separately.
Escape hatches can only count as one of the above-mentioned number of emergency exits.
Where 46 - 60 passengers and crew are accommodated in each compartment or deck, the minimum total number of exits shall be 6.
A double service door shall count as two doors.
A double or multiple window shall count as two emergency windows.

If the driver's compartment does not provide access to a passenger compartment by means of a passageway that permits (a) the front edge of the cylindrical gauge referred to in Annex 4, Figure 6 to reach at least the transverse vertical plane tangential to the foremost point of the driver's seat back in its rearmost longitudinal position, and (b) from this plane, to move the panel shown in Annex 4, Figure 7 forwards from the contact position, with the cylindrical gauge until it reaches at least the vertical plane tangential to the foremost point of the driver's seat cushion, then the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.1.7.1. to 7.6.1.7.5. shall be met.
Where the driver's compartment does not provide passenger-compartment access as described in paragraph 7.6.1.7., it shall have two exits, which shall not both be in the same lateral wall.
When one of the driver's compartment exits is a window, this window shall have a minimum area of 400,000 mm² and it shall be possible to inscribe in this area a rectangle measuring 500 mm x 700 mm.
When one of the driver's compartment exits is a window, it shall comply with the requirements set out in paragraph 7.6.8. for emergency windows.
Where one or two seats are fitted alongside the driver for additional people, both of the exits referred to in paragraph 7.6.1.7.1. shall be doors.

The driver's door shall be accepted as the emergency door for the occupants of the seats alongside the driver, provided that it is possible to move a test gauge from the occupants' seats to the exterior of the vehicle through the driver's door (see Annex 4, Figure 27).
The service door shall be in the side of the vehicle opposite to that containing the driver's door and shall be accepted as the emergency door for the driver.

In the circumstances described in paragraphs 7.6.1.7.1. and 7.6.1.7.2., the exits provided in the driver's compartment, and for the occupants of any seats alongside the driver, shall not count as one of the doors required by paragraphs 7.6.1.1. to 7.6.1.2., nor as one of the emergency exits required by paragraph 7.6.1.4. for any other passenger compartment.

Where up to five additional seats are fitted in a compartment incorporating the driver's compartment and any seats alongside the driver, the additional seats and the space for these seats shall comply with all requirements of this Regulation and at least one of the emergency exits required by paragraph 7.6.1.4. shall be a door giving access to the passenger compartment complying with the requirements of paragraph 7.6.3.1.2. for emergency doors.
Where a door or other barrier is fitted between the driver's seat and the passenger compartment, this barrier shall be capable of being released quickly by the driver in an emergency.
A driver's door in a compartment protected by such a barrier shall not be counted as an exit for passengers.
Vehicles of Classes II, III and B shall be fitted with escape hatches, additional to the emergency doors and windows.
Where the number of passengers (in the upper deck in the case of double-deck vehicles) exceeds 30, the minimum number of hatches shall be 2.

Hatches shall not be fitted in positions where technical components are installed which present possible danger to passengers using the escape hatches (e.g. high voltage systems, systems containing dangerous liquids and/or gas, etc.).
Vehicles of Classes I, II and III shall meet the requirements of paragraph 7.6.2.1.1. and its sub-paragraphs.

The service door(s) of Class I, II and III vehicles shall be situated on the side of the vehicle that is nearer to the side of the road corresponding to the direction of traffic for which the vehicle is designed and as declared by the manufacturer in the communication form of Annex 1, Part I, Appendix 1, paragraph 2.8., to this Regulation.
At least one of the service doors of Class I, II and III vehicles shall be in the forward half of the vehicle.

If the passenger compartment has an area S0 equal or greater than 10 m², two of the doors referred to in paragraph 7.6.1.1. shall be separated such that the distance between transverse vertical planes through their centres of area is not less than the distance given in paragraphs 7.6.2.3.1. and 7.6.2.3.2.

In the case of a single deck vehicle with a passenger compartment area S0 equal or greater than 10 m², two of the doors referred to in paragraph 7.6.1.1. shall be separated such that the distance between transverse vertical planes through their centres of area is not less than 40 per cent of the overall length of the passenger compartment measured parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

The exits (on each deck in the case of a double-deck vehicle) shall be placed in such a way that their number on each of the two sides of the vehicle is substantially the same; this shall not imply the need to provide additional exits over and above the number specified in paragraph 7.6.1.
At least one exit shall be situated either in the rear face or in the front face of the vehicle.
The exits on the same side of the vehicle shall be suitably separated along the length of the passenger compartment.

For vehicles of classes I, II and III, if there are two required escape hatches, they shall be separated by a distance of at least 2 m measured between the nearest edges of the apertures in a line parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
Vehicles of Class I, II or III shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.3.1.1. to 7.6.3.1.5.
Service doors shall have an aperture creating an access in accordance with the requirements shown in paragraph 7.7.1. of this annex.
Emergency doors shall have an aperture with a minimum height of 1,450 mm and a minimum width of 600 mm.
Emergency windows shall have a minimum area of 400,000 mm².
It shall be possible to inscribe in the area of an emergency window a rectangle measuring 500 mm x 700 mm.

In the case of an emergency window situated in the rear face of the vehicle, either it shall meet the requirements shown in paragraph 7.6.3.1.3., or it shall be possible to inscribe in the aperture of this emergency window a rectangle 350 mm high and 1,550 mm wide, the corners of which may be rounded to a radius of curvature not exceeding 250 mm.
Escape hatches shall have an aperture with a minimum area of 450,000 mm².
It shall be possible to inscribe in the aperture area of an escape hatch a rectangle measuring 600 mm x 700 mm.

Every service door shall be capable of being easily opened from inside and from outside the vehicle when the vehicle is stationary (but not necessarily when the vehicle is moving); this does not preclude locking the door from the outside, provided that the door can always be opened from the inside.
Every control or device for opening a service door from the outside shall be between 1,000 mm and 1,500 mm from the ground and not more than 500 mm from the door.

In vehicles of Classes I, II and III every control or device for opening a service door from the inside shall be between 1,000 mm and 1,500 mm from the upper surface of the floor or step nearest the control and be not more than 500 mm from the door, except that this shall not apply to controls located within the driver's area.

Every one-piece manually-operated service door which is hinged or pivoted shall be so hinged or pivoted that if the open door comes into contact with a stationary object while the vehicle is moving forwards it tends to close.
If a manually-operated service door is fitted with a slam lock, the slam lock shall be of the two-stage type.

On the inside of a service door there shall not be any device intended to cover the inside steps when the door is closed; this does not exclude the presence in the step well, when the door is closed, of the door operating mechanism and other equipment attached to the inside of the door which does not form an extension of the floor on which passengers may stand.
The door operating mechanism and other equipment attached to the inside of the service door in the step well should not be dangerous for the passengers.

If the direct view is not adequate, optical or other devices shall be installed to enable the driver to detect from his seat the presence of a passenger in the immediate interior and exterior vicinity of every side service door which is not an automatically-operated service door.
If driving mirrors are used to meet the requirements of paragraph 7.6.4.6, the field of view required for driving shall still be met.
Every door which opens towards the interior of the vehicle and its mechanism shall be so constructed that its movement is not likely to cause injury to passengers in normal conditions of use.
Where necessary, appropriate protection devices shall be fitted to every door which opens towards the interior of the vehicle and its mechanism.
The service door in any open position shall not obstruct the use of, or required access to, any mandatory exit.
If an overnight locking system is provided, the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.4.11.1 and 7.6.4.11.2 shall apply.

If an overnight locking system is provided, the locking system shall have been automatically deactivated when the ignition is in the "ON" position (or alternatively the warning of paragraph 7.6.4.11.2 shall be provided).

If an overnight locking system is provided and is not automatically deactivated when the ignition is in the "ON" position, a warning shall be provided to the driver indicating that the overnight locking system remains in operation at one or more door(s) when the ignition is in the "ON" position.

In the event of an emergency, every power-operated service door shall be capable, when the vehicle is stationary or driving at a speed less than or equal to 3 km/h, of being opened from inside and, when not locked, from outside by controls which, whether or not the power supply is operating, meet the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.5.1.1 to 7.6.5.1.9.
The emergency controls of every power-operated service door shall, whether or not the power supply is operating, override all other door controls.

In the case of interior emergency controls of a power-operated service door, the controls shall be placed on, or within 300 mm of, the door, at a height of not less than 1,000 mm above the first step (except in the case of interior controls for the door referred to in Annex 8, paragraph 3.9.1).
The emergency controls of every power-operated service door shall be capable of being easily seen and clearly identified when approaching the door and when standing in front of the door.
If the emergency controls of a power-operated service door are additional to the normal opening controls, they shall be clearly marked for emergency use.
The emergency controls of every power-operated service door shall be capable of being operated by one person when standing immediately in front of the door.

The emergency controls of every power-operated service door shall cause the door to open to a width that the gauge as defined in paragraph 7.7.1.1. below can pass through within 8 seconds after the operation of the control, or enable the door to be easily opened by hand to a width that the gauge as defined in paragraph 7.7.1.1. below can pass through within 8 seconds after the operation of the control.
The operation of the emergency control of a power-operated service door, or the removal of a protective cover over the control, shall be indicated to the driver both audibly and visually.

In the case of a driver-operated power-operated service door which does not comply with the requirements of paragraph 7.6.5.6.2., the emergency controls shall be such that after they have been operated to open the door and returned to their normal position, the door will not close again until the driver subsequently operates a closing control.
In the case of interior emergency controls of a power-operated service door, the controls shall be deactivated if the vehicle moves at a speed higher than 3 km/h.

If a device is provided to deactivate the outside emergency controls, the outside emergency controls shall be reactivated automatically either by the starting of the engine or before the vehicle reaches a speed of 20 km/h.

If a device is provided to deactivate the outside emergency controls, subsequent deactivation of the outside emergency controls shall not occur automatically, but shall require a further action by the driver.

Every driver-operated service door shall be capable of operation by the driver when in the driving seat using controls which, except in the case of a foot control, are clearly and distinctively marked.

Every power-operated service door shall activate a visual tell-tale, which shall be plainly visible to the driver when seated in the normal driving position in any normal ambient lighting condition, to warn that a door is not fully closed.
The tell-tale of a power-operated service door shall signal whenever the rigid structure of the door is between the fully open position and a point 30 mm from the fully closed position.
No such tell-tale shall be fitted in respect of a front service door which does not comply with the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.5.6.1.1. and 7.6.5.6.1.2. below.

Where controls are provided for the driver to open and close a power-operated service door, they shall be such that the driver is able to reverse the movement of the door at any time during the closing or opening process.
The construction and control system of every power-operated service door shall be such that a passenger is unlikely to be injured by the door or trapped in the door as it closes.

When the closing of a power-operated service door at any measuring point described in Annex 6 is resisted by a clamping force not exceeding 150 N, the door shall reopen automatically to its fullest extent and, except in the case of an automatically-operated service door, remain open until a closing control is operated.
The peak clamping force may be higher than 150 N for a short time provided that it does not exceed 300 N.
Whenever the doors of a power-operated service door are closed onto the wrist or fingers of a passenger, one of the conditions of paragraphs 7.6.5.6.1.2.1 to 7.6.5.6.1.2.3 shall be met.

Whenever the doors are closed onto the wrist or fingers of a passenger, the door shall reopen automatically to its fullest extent and, except in the case of an automatically-operated service door, remain open until a closing control is operated (or paragraph 7.6.5.6.1.2.2 or 7.6.5.6.1.2.3 shall be met).

Whenever the doors are closed onto the wrist or fingers of a passenger, the wrist or fingers shall be capable of being readily extracted from the doors without risk of injury to the passenger (or paragraph 7.6.5.6.1.2.1 or 7.6.5.6.1.2.3 shall be met).
If the door traps the test bar, the bar shall be capable of being easily removed.

Whenever the doors are closed onto the wrist or fingers of a passenger, the door shall be maintained at a position allowing the free passage of a test bar having a section of height 60 mm, width 20 mm, with corners radiused to 5 mm (or paragraph 7.6.5.6.1.2.1 or 7.6.5.6.1.2.2 shall be met).
The position at which the door is maintained shall not be more than 30 mm distant from the fully closed position.
In the case of a front service door, the door shall fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.5.6.1.1. and 7.6.5.6.1.2. (or be fitted with soft edges in accordance with paragraph 7.6.5.6.2.2).

In the case of a front service door, the door may be fitted with soft edges instead of fulfilling paragraphs 7.6.5.6.1.1 and 7.6.5.6.1.2; the soft edges shall not be so soft that if the doors are closed on the test bar mentioned in paragraph 7.6.5.6.1.1. the rigid structure of the doors will reach the fully closed position.

Where a power-operated service door is held closed only by the continued application of the power supply, a visual warning device shall be provided to inform the driver of any failure in the power supply to the doors.
A starting prevention device, if fitted, shall be effective only at speeds of less than 5 km/h and shall be incapable of operation above that speed.

If the vehicle is not fitted with a starting prevention device, an audible warning to the driver shall be activated if the vehicle is driven away from rest when any power-operated service door is not fully closed.
The audible warning shall be activated at a speed exceeding 5 km/h for doors complying with the requirements of paragraph 7.6.5.6.1.2.3.
Except as provided in paragraph 7.6.5.1., the opening controls of every automatically-operated service door shall be capable of being activated and deactivated only by the driver from his seat.

Activation of the opening controls of an automatically-operated service door by the driver shall be indicated inside and, where a door is to be opened from outside, also on the outside of the vehicle.
The indicator of activation of the opening controls (e.g. illuminated push-button, illuminated sign) shall be on or adjacent to the door to which it relates.

In the case of direct actuation by means of a switch, the functional state of the system shall be clearly indicated to the driver, by, for example, the position of the switch or an indicator lamp or an illuminated switch.
In the case of direct actuation by means of a switch, the switch shall be specially marked and arranged in such a way that it cannot be confused with other controls.

After activation of the opening controls of an automatically-operated service door by the driver, it shall be possible for passengers to open the door as set out in paragraphs 7.6.6.2.1.1 and 7.6.6.2.1.2.

After activation of the opening controls by the driver, it shall be possible for passengers to open an automatically-operated service door from inside, for example by pressing a push-button or passing a light barrier.

After activation of the opening controls by the driver, it shall be possible for passengers to open an automatically-operated service door from outside, except in the case of a door intended only as an exit and marked as such, by, for example, pressing an illuminated push-button, a push-button beneath an illuminated sign, or a similar device marked with a suitable instruction.
When an automatically-operated service door has opened, it shall close again automatically after a time interval has elapsed.

If a passenger enters or leaves the vehicle during the time interval before an automatically-operated service door closes, a safety device (e.g. a footboard contact, light barrier, one-way gate) shall ensure that the time until the door closes is sufficiently extended.

If a passenger enters or leaves the vehicle while an automatically-operated service door is closing, the closing process shall be interrupted automatically and the door shall return to the open position.

A door that has closed automatically in accordance with paragraph 7.6.6.3.1. shall be capable of being opened again by a passenger in accordance with paragraph 7.6.6.2.; this shall not apply if the driver has deactivated the opening controls.
After deactivation of the opening controls of the automatically-operated service doors by the driver, open doors shall close in accordance with paragraphs 7.6.6.3.1. and 7.6.6.3.2.
For automatically-operated service doors marked for special service, the driver shall be able to inhibit the automatic closing process by actuation of a special control.
For automatically-operated service doors marked for special service, a passenger shall also be able to inhibit the automatic closing process directly by pressing a special push-button.
The inhibition of the automatic closing process on doors marked for special service shall be indicated to the driver, e.g. by a visual tell-tale.
Re-establishment of the automatic closing process on doors marked for special service shall in any case be capable of being done by the driver.
Paragraph 7.6.6.3. shall apply to the subsequent closing of a door on which the automatic closing process has been inhibited.

Emergency doors shall be capable of being easily opened from inside and from outside when the vehicle is stationary; this does not preclude locking the door from the outside, provided that the door can always be opened from the inside by the use of the normal opening mechanism.

Emergency doors, during their use as such, shall not be of the power-operated type unless, once either a service door control prescribed in paragraph 7.6.5.1. or a control for a dedicated emergency door complying with the provisions of paragraph 7.6.5.1. has been actuated and returned to its normal position, the doors do not close again until the driver subsequently operates a closing control.

Activation of one of the controls prescribed in paragraph 7.6.5.1. shall cause an emergency door to open to a width that the gauge as defined in paragraph 7.7.2.1. below can pass through within a maximum of 8 seconds after the operation of the control, or enable the door to be easily opened by hand to a width that the gauge can pass through within a maximum of 8 seconds after the operation of the control.
Emergency doors shall not be of the sliding type except in the case of vehicles having a capacity not exceeding 22 passengers.

Every control or device for opening an emergency door (on the lower deck in the case of a double-deck vehicle) from the outside shall be between 1,000 mm and 1,500 mm from the ground and not more than 500 mm from the door.

In vehicles of Classes I, II and III every control or device for opening an emergency door from the inside shall be between 1,000 mm and 1,500 mm from the upper surface of the floor or step nearest to the control and be not more than 500 mm from the door, except that this shall not apply to controls located within the driver's area.
Hinged emergency doors fitted to the side of the vehicle shall be hinged at their forward edge and shall open outwards.

Check straps, chains or other restraining devices on hinged side emergency doors shall not prevent the door from opening to, and remaining open at, an angle of at least 100 degrees; if a means is provided sufficient to give free passage to the emergency door access gauge, the 100 degrees minimum angle requirement shall not apply.

Emergency doors shall be proofed against unintentional operation, except that this requirement shall not apply if the emergency door is locked automatically when the vehicle is moving at a speed exceeding 5 km/h.
All emergency doors shall be provided with an audible device to warn the driver when they are not securely closed.
The audible warning device of an emergency door shall be operated by movement of the door catch or handle and not by movement of the door itself.
If an overnight locking system is provided, the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.7.7.1 and 7.6.7.7.2 shall apply.

If an overnight locking system is provided, the locking system shall have been automatically deactivated when the ignition is in the "ON" position (or alternatively the warning of paragraph 7.6.7.7.2 shall be provided).
Every emergency window shall either meet the requirements of paragraph 7.6.8.2.1. or meet the requirements of paragraph 7.6.8.2.2.
Where an emergency window meets paragraph 7.6.8.2.2., it shall be made of toughened glass pane(s), which precludes the use of panes of laminated glass or of plastic material.

An easy-to-operate device shall ensure that each glass pane of the toughened glass emergency window can be broken and removed within 20 seconds by a single person from inside the passenger compartment.
The device for breaking and removing the toughened glass pane(s) of the emergency window shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.8.2.2.1. to 7.6.8.2.2.5.
The device shall be fixed adjacent to or on the emergency window and positioned in the upper third of the height of the window surface.
In case of an emergency window at the rear of the vehicle the device shall be fixed centrally adjacent to or on the window or, alternatively, positioned adjacent to or on both sides of the window.
In case the implementation of the device is not technically compatible with the positional requirements above, the device shall be located adjacent to or affixed on each emergency window.
The device shall be clearly visible for any passenger in its direct vicinity.
The device shall be marked in red and supplemented by a safety sign.
The device shall be readily available at all times.

In case of electronic devices, such device shall be operational in the event of a failure of the vehicle's power supply, and its operational status shall be easily verifiable at the driver’s seat position.
The device shall be designed to prevent misuse.

At least one of the following mitigating measures, at the manufacturer's choice, shall be available: the device shall (a) be permanently fixed adjacent to or on each emergency window; or (b) engage a warning signal being audible or visible at the driver's seating position when the device is temporarily removed from its designated location.
The device shall be equipped with a protective cover or designed to prevent unintended operation and shall require one additional action to unlock by any person operating the device.
If a protective cover is used, the device shall remain visible by passengers.
Where a plastic film is fitted to an emergency window, the plastic film shall be cut at the outer edge of the emergency window and following a pattern e.g., shown in Annex 4, Figure 32.
In case of fitting a plastic film to the emergency exit, it shall be compatible with the device and shall not reduce its efficiency.
Where a plastic film is fitted, the characteristics of the approved glazing shall remain unchanged.
Every emergency window which can be locked from the outside shall be so constructed as to be capable of being opened at all times from inside the vehicle.

The height of the lower edge of an emergency window made of breakable glass fitted in the side of the vehicle, from the general level of the floor immediately below it (excluding any local variations such as the presence of a wheel or transmission housing), shall be not more than 1,200 mm nor less than 500 mm.
Every escape hatch shall operate so as not to obstruct the clear passage from inside or outside the vehicle.
Roof escape hatches shall be ejectable, hinged or made of readily-breakable safety glass.
Ejectable types of escape hatch shall not become totally detached from the vehicle when operated such that the hatch is not a danger to other road users.
The operation of ejectable escape hatches shall be such that inadvertent operation is effectively prevented.
Hinged escape hatches shall hinge along the edge towards the front or rear of the vehicle and shall hinge through an angle of at least 100 degrees.

Escape hatches shall be capable of being easily opened or removed from the inside and from the outside, without precluding locking of the escape hatch for securing the vehicle when unattended, provided that the escape hatch can always be opened or removed from the inside by the use of the normal opening or removal mechanism.

In the case of a hatch made of or with toughened glass pane(s), an easy-to-operate device shall ensure that each glass pane(s) can be broken and removed within 20 sec by a single person from inside the passenger compartment.
The device for breaking and removing the toughened glass pane(s) of the escape hatch shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.9.5.1. to 7.6.9.5.3.4.

At least one of the following mitigating measures, at the manufacturer's choice, shall be available: the device shall (a) be permanently fixed adjacent to or on each escape hatch; or (b) engage a warning signal being audible or visible at the driver's seating position, when the device is temporarily removed from its designated location.
Where a plastic film is fitted to an escape hatch, the plastic film shall be cut at the outer edge of the emergency window and following a pattern as e.g. shown in Annex 4, Figure 32.
Retractable steps, if fitted, shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.10.1. to 7.6.10.9.
When the door is closed, no part of the retractable step shall project more than 10 mm beyond the adjacent line of the body work.
When the door is open and the retractable step is in the extended position, the surface area shall conform to the requirements of paragraph 7.7.7. of this annex.
In the case of a power-operated retractable step, it shall not be possible for the vehicle to move from rest, under its own power, when the step is in the extended position.
In the case of a manually operated retractable step, an audible indication shall alert the driver when the step is not fully retracted.
A power-operated retractable step shall not be capable of being extended when the vehicle is in motion.
If the device to operate the power-operated step fails, the step shall retract and remain in the retracted position.
The operation of the corresponding door shall not be hindered in the event of failure of the device operating the power-operated step or by the step being damaged or obstructed.
When a passenger is standing on a power-operated retractable step, the corresponding door shall be incapable of being closed, except for any door within the driver’s direct field of view.
Compliance with the requirement that the door be incapable of closing shall be checked by placing a mass of 15 kg, representing a small child, at the centre of the step.
The corners of retractable steps facing forwards or rearwards shall be rounded to a radius of not less than 5 mm.
The edges of retractable steps shall be rounded to a radius of not less than 2.5 mm.
When the passenger door is open, the retractable step shall be securely held in the extended position.

When a mass of 136 kg is placed in the centre of a single retractable step or a mass of 272 kg is placed in the centre of a double retractable step, the deflection at any point on the step, measured relative to the body of vehicle, shall not exceed 10 mm.
All safety signs shall comply with requirements contained in paragraph 6.5. of ISO standard 3864-1:2011.
Each safety sign required by this Regulation shall be used to communicate only one safety message.
The information provided on each safety sign shall be in the form of pictograms; words, letters and numbers may supplement the pictogram in combination on the same sign.
Each safety sign shall be located and orientated so as to be easily understood.

Safety signs shall follow the principles shown in the example layouts, i.e. a header section depicting the safety message, a second section containing instructional information and a third, optional, footer section for non-critical text.
Pictograms indicating required actions by the user shall show a person, or the relevant part of a person, operating the equipment or device.
Pictograms indicating a required movement shall, where appropriate, show an arrow pointing in the direction of motion.
Where a rotational movement is required, a curved arrow shall be used in the pictogram.
Where devices are to be operated, panels removed or doors opened, the pictogram shall indicate the action in progress.
The lower case letter(s) of supplementary words, single letters and numbers on safety signs shall have a minimum height of 8 mm.
Words on safety signs shall not be in upper case letters only.

All safety signs that are visible from the inside of the vehicle shall be of photo-luminescent material having luminance decay characteristics conforming, as a minimum, to sub-classification C in Table 2 of ISO Standard 17398:2004, when measured in accordance with paragraph 7.11. of that standard.

Safety signs shall not be located in positions where they may be obscured during operation of the vehicle, except that a curtain or blind may be positioned over an emergency window provided an additional safety sign indicates that the emergency window is located behind the curtain or blind.
Each emergency exit, and any other exit that meets the prescriptions for an emergency exit, shall be marked by one of the relevant pictograms described in Table 3 of ISO Standard 7010:2011.
The pictograms marking each emergency exit, and any other exit that meets the prescriptions for an emergency exit, shall be legible from both the inside and the outside of the vehicle.
Safety signs shall be positioned adjacent to, or surround, or be on, all internal and external emergency controls and device(s) for breaking emergency window(s).
No part of a safety sign shall obscure any misuse protection that may be present, e.g. a cover.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 7.6.12.2.1. to 7.6.12.2.5.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall be of white colour.

Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall illuminate a flat, horizontal portion of the ground having a width of 2 m measured from a plane parallel to the median longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle which passes through the outermost point of the closed service door and over a length extending from a transverse plane which passes through the foremost edge of the closed service door to a transverse plane passing through the centre line of the foremost wheels situated to the rear of the service door, or, in the case where there are no such wheels, to a transverse plane passing through the rear of the vehicle.

Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall have limited dazzle outside a zone on the ground having a maximum width of 5 m measured from the side of the vehicle and a maximum length limited by a transverse plane passing through the front of the vehicle and a transverse plane passing through the rear of the vehicle.

If the lower edge of the service-door lighting device is less than 2 m from the ground, the device shall not project more than 50 mm beyond the overall width of the vehicle measured without this device.
If the lower edge of the service-door lighting device is less than 2 m from the ground, the device shall have radii of curvature of not less than 2.5 mm.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall be installed so that the device can only be switched on when a service door is operated and the vehicle speed does not exceed 5 km/h.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall be installed so that it is switched off automatically before the vehicle reaches a speed exceeding 5 km/h.

The free space extending inwards into the vehicle from the side wall in which the service door is mounted shall permit the free passage of one test gauge having the dimensions of either test gauge 1 or test gauge 2 specified in Annex 4, Figure 1.

Between the cylindrical figure, at the position set out in paragraph 7.7.1.4., and the dual panel, at the position set out in paragraph 7.7.1.3., there shall be a free space whose upper and lower limits are shown in Annex 4, Figure 2, and this free space shall permit the free passage of a vertical panel whose form and dimensions are the same as the cylindrical form (paragraph 7.7.5.1.), central section and a thickness of no more than 20 mm.

The free passage clearance for the figure shall not include any space extending to 300 mm in front of any uncompressed seat cushion of a forward or rearward facing seat, or 225 mm in the case of sideways-facing seats and to the height of the top of the seat cushion (see Annex 4, Figure 25).
The maximum slope of the floor in the access passage shall not exceed 5 per cent.
The surface of access passages shall be slip-resistant.

Except as provided for in paragraph 7.7.2.4., the free space between the gangway and the emergency door aperture shall permit the free passage of a vertical cylinder 300 mm in diameter and 700 mm high from the floor and supporting a second vertical cylinder 550 mm in diameter, the aggregate height of the assembly being 1,400 mm.
It shall be possible to move a test gauge from the gangway to the exterior of the vehicle through every emergency window.

Except in the case of Class I and A vehicles, at least one roof escape hatch shall be located such that a four-sided truncated pyramid having a side angle of 20 degrees and a height of 1,600 mm touches part of a seat or equivalent support.
Supports may be foldable or movable provided they can be locked in their position of use, and this position shall be taken for verification.

The gangway(s) of the vehicle shall be so designed and constructed as to permit the free passage of a gauging device consisting of two co-axial cylinders with an inverted truncated cone interposed between them, the gauging device having the dimensions shown in Annex 4, Figure 6.

In vehicles of Classes II, III and B, where the gauging device according to Annex 4, Figure 6 comes into contact with a monitor or display device mounted from the ceiling above the gangway, the maximum force necessary to move any such monitor or display device out of the way, in both directions, shall not exceed 35 Newton.
After being moved out of the way, the monitor or display device shall maintain its position and not automatically redeploy.

If there is no exit forward of a seat or row of seats, in the case of forward-facing seats, the front edge of the cylindrical gauge defined in paragraph 7.7.5.1. shall reach at least until the transverse vertical plane tangential to the foremost point of the foremost front row seat back and be retained in that position.

If there is no exit forward of a seat or row of seats, in the case of forward-facing seats, from the transverse vertical plane it shall be possible to move the panel shown in Annex 4, Figure 7, in such a way that starting from the contact position with the cylindrical gauge, the panel side facing the exterior of the vehicle is displaced forwards a distance of 660 mm.

On vehicles of Class III where the seats on one side or on both sides of the gangway are movable laterally so that the gangway width is reduced to a figure corresponding to a lower cylinder diameter of 220 mm, the operation of a control on each seat, readily accessible to a person standing in the gangway, shall be sufficient to cause the seat to return easily and, if possible, automatically, even when it is loaded, to the position corresponding to a minimum width of 300 mm.
The width of steps fitted in the gangways shall not be less than the width of the gangway at the top of the steps.
Folding seats allowing passengers to sit in the gangway shall not be fitted.
Folding seats in other areas of the vehicle shall not obstruct the passage down the gangway of the gangway test gauge when in the open (seating) position.
Laterally-sliding seats which in one position encroach on the gangway shall not be fitted except on vehicles of Class III and subject to the conditions prescribed in paragraph 7.7.5.3.
The surface of gangways shall be slip-resistant.
The slope of the gangway shall not exceed the values given in paragraphs 7.7.6.1. and 7.7.6.2.
The slope of the gangway in the longitudinal direction shall not exceed 12.5 per cent in the case of a vehicle of Classes III and B.
The slope of the gangway in the transversal direction shall not exceed 5 per cent for all classes.

The height and depth of steps for passengers at service and emergency doors, and within the vehicle, shall be within the maximum and minimum height and the minimum depth specified in Annex 4, Figure 8.
The vertical distance between the gangway surface and the floor of the seating area shall not exceed 350 mm.

Where there is more than one step, each step may extend into the area of the vertical projection of the next step by up to 100 mm and the projection over the tread below shall leave a free surface of at least 200 mm (see Annex 4, figure 8).
Where there is more than one step, all step nosings shall be designed such as to minimize the risk of tripping.

The width and shape of every step shall be such that a rectangle as indicated in the table of paragraph 7.7.7.5. can be placed on that step with not more than 5 per cent of the area of the appropriate rectangle overhanging the step.

At a double doorway each half of the doorway shall fulfil the requirement that a rectangle as indicated in the table of paragraph 7.7.7.5. can be placed on every step with not more than 5 per cent of its area overhanging the step.
For vehicles with a number of passengers > 22, the first step shall accommodate a rectangle of 400 x 300 mm.
For vehicles with a number of passengers > 22, the other steps shall accommodate a rectangle of 400 x 200 mm.
All steps shall have a slip-resistant surface.
The maximum slope of the step in any direction shall not exceed 5 per cent.

All step nosings shall have a band of contrasting colour on the front edge of the tread, 20-50 mm wide, providing either a visual contrast of C ≥ 0.7 and a diffuse reflectance ρd of at least 0.5 according to Annex 5 of the step nosing (object to be seen) or being black on yellow or yellow on black or black on white or white on black.

The minimum width of the seat cushion, dimension "F" (Annex 4, Figure 9), measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of that seating position, shall be as specified in paragraphs 7.7.8.1.1.1. and 7.7.8.1.1.2.
The minimum width of the seat cushion, dimension "F" (Annex 4, Figure 9), measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of that seating position, shall be 225 mm in the case of Class III.

The minimum width of the available space for each seating position, dimension "G" (Annex 4, Figure 9), measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of that seating position at height between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed seat cushion, shall be not less than the values in paragraphs 7.7.8.1.2.1. and 7.7.8.1.2.2.

The minimum width of the available space for each seating position, dimension "G" (Annex 4, Figure 9), measured from a vertical plane through the centre of that seating position at height between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed seat cushion, shall be not less than 250 mm in the case of individual seats.

The minimum width of the available space for each seating position, dimension "G" (Annex 4, Figure 9), measured from a vertical plane through the centre of that seating position at height between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed seat cushion, shall be not less than 225 mm in the case of continuous rows of seats for two or more passengers.

For vehicles not exceeding a width of 2.35 m, the width of the available space for each seating position, measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of that seating position at heights between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed seat cushion, shall be 200 mm (see Annex 4, Figure 9A); in case of compliance with this paragraph the requirements of paragraph 7.7.8.1.2. shall not apply.

For vehicles not exceeding a width of 2.35 m, in the case of vehicles of Class III, the minimum width of the seat cushion, dimension "F" (Annex 4, Figure 9A), measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of that seating position, shall be a minimum of 200 mm; in case of compliance with this paragraph the requirements of paragraph 7.7.8.1.1.2. shall not apply.
The minimum depth of a seat cushion (dimension K, Annex 4, Figure 11) shall be as specified in paragraphs 7.7.8.2.1. and 7.7.8.2.2.
The minimum depth of a seat cushion (dimension K, Annex 4, Figure 11) shall be 400 mm in vehicles of Class II or Class III.

The height of the uncompressed seat cushion (dimension H, Annex 4, Figure 11a) relative to the floor shall be such that the distance from the floor to a horizontal plane tangential to the front upper surface of the seat cushion is between 400 mm and 500 mm, except that this height may be reduced to not less than 350 mm at the wheel arches (taking into account the allowances permitted in paragraph 7.7.8.5.2.) and at the engine/transmission compartment.

For seats facing in the same direction in Classes II and III, the distance between the front of a seat squab and the back of the squab of the seat preceding it (dimension H), measured horizontally, parallel to the longitudinal plane of the vehicle and at all heights above the floor between the level of the top surface of the seat cushion and a point 620 mm above the floor, shall not be less than 680 mm.

For a seat behind a partition or other rigid structure other than a seat, a minimum clear space in front of each required passenger seating space (as defined in paragraph 7.7.8.6.) shall be provided as shown in Annex 4, Figure 13.

For a seat behind a seat and/or a seat facing the gangway, a minimum clear foot space of at least 300 mm depth and a width according to paragraph 7.7.8.1.1. of this annex shall be provided as shown in Annex 4, Figure 11b.
The local presence in the foot space of seat legs, passenger footrests and of intrusions as provided by paragraph 7.7.8.6. is permitted provided that adequate space remains for the passengers’ feet.
The foot space may partly be situated in and/or above the gangway but shall not create any obstruction when measuring the minimum gangway-width in accordance with paragraph 7.7.5.
In the case of vehicles of Class III subject to the requirements of Annex 8, the minimum number of priority seats shall be two in Class III.
A seat that folds out of the way when not in use shall not be designated as a priority seat.

In the case of single deck vehicles, over each seating position and its associated foot space (except for the seat(s) alongside the driver in a vehicle of Class A or B), there shall be a free space with a height of not less than 900 mm measured from the highest point of the uncompressed seat cushion and at least 1,350 mm from the mean level of the floor in the foot space; for vehicles to which paragraph 7.7.1.10. applies, and for the seat(s) alongside the driver in a vehicle of Class A or B, these dimensions may be reduced to 1,200 mm measured from the floor and 800 mm measured from the highest point of the uncompressed seat cushion.
The free space defined in paragraph 7.7.8.6.1. shall be extended over the zone defined in paragraphs 7.7.8.6.2.1. and 7.7.8.6.2.2.
The free space shall extend over the zone defined by longitudinal vertical planes 200 mm either side of the median vertical plane of the seating position.

The free space shall extend over the zone defined by a transverse vertical plane through the rearmost upper point of the seat back and by a transverse vertical plane 280 mm in front of the foremost point of the uncompressed seat cushion, measured in each case at the median vertical plane of the seating position.

The driver shall be protected from standing passengers and from passengers seated immediately behind the driver's compartment who may be projected into the driver's compartment in the event of braking or cornering.
Where a guard is fitted, it shall comply with the requirements specified in paragraphs 7.7.13.1.2.1. to 7.7.13.1.2.3. (see Annex 4, Figure 30).
Where a guard is fitted, the minimum height of the guard measured from the floor on which the passenger's feet rest shall be 800 mm.

Where a guard is fitted, its width shall extend inwards from the wall of the vehicle at least as far as 100 mm beyond the longitudinal centre line of the innermost relevant passenger seat, but in any case shall extend at least as far as the innermost point of the driver's seat.
Where a guard is fitted, the distance between the uppermost edge of an area destined to hold any object (e.g. a table) and the uppermost edge of the guard shall be at least 90 mm.
The driver's compartment shall be protected from objects liable to roll into it from the passenger area immediately behind the compartment in the case of heavy braking.
The driver shall be protected from the sun and from the effects of glare and reflections caused by artificial interior lighting.
Any lighting likely to affect adversely and significantly the driver's vision shall be capable of being operated only while the vehicle is at rest.
The vehicle shall be provided with devices allowing defrosting and demisting of the windscreen.
The driver's seat shall be independent of other seats.

The driver's seat back shall either be curved or the driver's area shall be provided with armrests positioned in such a way that the driver is neither constrained during vehicle manoeuvring operations, nor becomes unbalanced by transverse accelerations which can occur in service.

The minimum width of the driver's seat cushion (dimension F, see Annex 4, Figure 9) measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of the seat shall be as specified in paragraphs 7.7.14.3.1. and 7.7.14.3.2.
The minimum width of the driver's seat cushion (dimension F), measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of the seat, shall be 225 mm in the case of Class I, II or III.

The minimum depth of the driver's seat cushion (dimension K, see Annex 4, Figure 11a) measured from a vertical plane passing through the centre of the seat shall be as specified in paragraphs 7.7.14.4.1. and 7.7.14.4.2.
The minimum depth of the driver's seat cushion (dimension K) shall be 400 mm in the case of Class I, II or III.
The minimum overall width of the driver's seat back measured up to a height of 250 mm above the horizontal plane tangential to the uppermost surface of the uncompressed seat cushion shall be 450 mm.
The distance between armrests shall ensure a free space for the driver, as defined in paragraph 7.7.14.2., of not less than 450 mm.
The driver's seat shall be adjustable in its longitudinal and vertical positions and in its seat back inclination.
The driver's seat shall lock automatically in the selected position.
If the driver's seat is fitted with a swivelling mechanism, it shall lock automatically when in the driving position.
The driver's seat shall be equipped with a suspension system.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of the items listed in paragraphs 7.8.1.1. to 7.8.1.6.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of all passenger compartments, crew compartments, toilet compartments and the articulated section of an articulated vehicle.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of any step or steps.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of the access to any exits and the area immediately around the service door(s) including, when in use, any boarding device fitted.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of the internal markings and internal controls of all exits.
Internal electrical lighting shall be provided for the illumination of all places where there are obstacles.

The vehicle shall have at least two internal lighting circuits such that failure of one will not affect the other; a circuit serving only permanent entry and exit lighting can be considered as one of these circuits.
Vehicles of Classes II, III and B shall be equipped with an emergency lighting system meeting paragraphs 7.8.3.1. to 7.8.3.10.
On vehicles of Classes II, III and B, it shall be possible for the driver to activate the emergency lighting system from the driver's seating position.
On vehicles of Classes II, III and B, the operation of the emergency control of any service or emergency door shall activate the emergency lighting system.
The emergency lighting system, once activated, shall remain active for at least 30 minutes unless de-activated by the driver.
The power supply for the emergency lighting shall be suitably located within the vehicle to minimise the risk of its continued operation being prejudiced as the result of an accident.
All units providing the emergency lighting shall produce a white light.
The uniformity of illuminance of the emergency lighting shall be assessed in accordance with the measures in paragraphs 7.8.3.7. to 7.8.3.10.

The emergency lighting system shall provide a minimum illuminance of 10 lux directly under each light unit in the passenger compartment at a height of 750 mm above the centreline of all access passages and gangways.
The uniformity of the illuminance of the emergency lighting over the length of the passenger compartment at a height of 750 mm above all access passages and gangways shall be between 0.15 and 2.
The emergency lighting system shall provide a minimum illuminance of 1 lux at floor level in the centreline of all access passages and gangways and at the centre of any step, at step level.

Conformity with the uniformity requirements of the emergency lighting shall be demonstrated over a period of at least 30 minutes from initiation of the emergency lighting by measurements taken at distances not exceeding 2 metres.
Control of the mandatory interior lighting shall be by manual switches under the control of the driver or automatically controlled.
Handrails and handholds shall be of adequate strength.
Handrails and handholds shall be so designed and installed as to present no risk of injury to passengers.
Handrails and handholds shall be of a section enabling passengers to grasp them easily and firmly.
Every handrail shall provide a length of at least 100 mm to accommodate a hand.

No dimension of the section of handrails and handholds shall be smaller than 20 mm or greater than 45 mm except in the case of handrails on doors and seats and, in the case of a vehicle of Class II, III or B, in access passages; in these cases handrails having a minimum dimension of 15 mm shall be permitted provided that one other dimension is of at least 25 mm.
Handrails shall not have sharp bends.

The clearance between a hand-rail or hand-hold, along the majority of its length, and the adjacent part of the vehicle body or walls shall be at least 40 mm; however, in the case of a handrail on a door or a seat, or in the access passage of a vehicle of Class II, III or B, a minimum clearance of 35 mm shall be permitted.

The surface of every handrail, handhold or stanchion shall contrast visually with their immediate surroundings and have a diffuse reflectance ρd of at least 0.5 according to Annex 5 or be yellow or white.
The surface of every handrail, handhold or stanchion shall be slip-resistant.
Door apertures shall be fitted with handrails and/or handholds on each side; in the case of double doors this requirement can be fulfilled by fitting one central stanchion or one central handrail.

Handrails and/or handholds provided for service doors shall include a grasping point available to a person standing on the ground adjacent to the service door or on any of the successive steps, situated vertically between 800 mm and 1,100 mm above the ground or above the surface of each step, and horizontally as specified in paragraphs 7.11.3.2.1. and 7.11.3.2.2.

For the position appropriate to a person standing on the ground, the grasping point of the service door handrail or handhold shall be not more than 400 mm inwards from the outer edge of the first step.

For the position appropriate to a particular step, the grasping point of the service door handrail or handhold shall be not outwards from the outer edge of the step considered, and not more than 600 mm inwards from that same edge.

Where any seated passenger is likely to be thrown forward into a step well, designated wheelchair space, pram space or open area for standing passengers as a result of heavy braking, a guard shall be fitted (or, in the case of a vehicle of Class A or B, a safety-belt).

Where fitted, the guard shall have a minimum height from the floor on which the passenger's feet rest of 800 mm and shall extend inwards from the wall of the vehicle at least as far as 100 mm beyond the longitudinal centre line of any seating position where the passenger is at risk or, in the case of a step well, to the riser of the innermost step, whichever is the lesser.
The occupants of the vehicle shall be protected from objects liable to fall from baggage racks under braking or cornering forces.
If baggage compartments are fitted, they shall be designed in such a way that baggage is prevented from falling in the event of sudden braking.
If fitted, every trap door that is not an escape hatch on the floor of a vehicle shall be so fitted and secured that it cannot be dislodged or opened without the use of tools or keys.
If a floor trap door that is not an escape hatch is fitted, no lifting or securing device shall project by more than eight mm above floor level.
If a floor trap door that is not an escape hatch is fitted, edges of projections shall be rounded.
Forms of visual entertainment for passengers, for example television monitors or videos, shall be located out of the driver's view when the driver is seated in his normal driving position.

In the case of vehicles of Classes II non low floor, III and B, the means to transmit safety information shall be adapted to the design and architecture of the vehicle with the aim of making the safety instructions easily accessible and intelligible from any passenger seat.
For access to service doors of a Class III vehicle, the height of the upper panel (dimension "A", Figure 1) shall be 850 mm for test gauge 1 and 1,100 mm for test gauge 2.

For a single-deck Class III vehicle, the gangway gauging device shall have B = 450 mm, C = 300 mm (220 mm for laterally movable seats, see paragraph 7.7.5.3. of Annex 3), D = 500 mm, E = 1,900 mm and F = 900 mm, subject to the footnoted reductions (footnotes 1 and 4).

For Classes II, III and B, the first step from the ground ("D") shall have a maximum height of 380 mm (700 mm in the case of an emergency door; 430 mm in the case of a vehicle with solely mechanical suspension; 380 mm for at least one service door and 400 mm for other service doors).
The first step from the ground ("D") shall have a minimum depth of 300 mm.
For Classes II, III and B, the other steps ("E") shall have a maximum height of 350 mm (250 mm in gangways for vehicles having a capacity not exceeding 22 passengers).
The other steps ("E") shall have a minimum height of 120 mm.
The other steps ("E") shall have a minimum depth of 200 mm.
At a double doorway, the steps in each half of the access passage shall be treated separately.
For passenger seats, the minimum dimension G shall be 225 mm for continuous seats and 250 mm for individual seats where F is at least 200 mm (225 mm for Class III).
For Classes II and III, the dimension H of the seat spacing shall be 680 mm.
In vehicles of Classes II and III, the seat-cushion dimension K (Figure 11a) shall be 400 mm minimum.
Every piece of safety glazing material, including the samples and test pieces submitted for approval, shall bear a trade name or mark of the manufacturer as listed under item 3 of Annex 1.
Manufactured parts of safety glazing material shall bear the ECE Regulation No. 43 number allocated to the prime manufacturer.
The marking on safety glazing material (trade name or mark and ECE Regulation No. 43 number) shall be clearly legible and indelible.

An international approval mark shall be affixed conspicuously to every piece of glazing and multiple-glazed unit conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, in addition to the marking prescribed in paragraph 4.1.
The international approval mark shall consist of the elements in paragraphs 5.4.1. and 5.4.2.
The approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval mark shall consist of the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 5.4.1.
The additional symbols listed in paragraphs 5.5.1. to 5.5.13. shall be affixed near the approval mark, as applicable.
The symbol V shall be affixed near the approval mark in the case of safety glazing having a regular light transmittance less than 70 per cent.
All glazing materials, including glazing material for the manufacture of windscreens, shall be such that, in the event of shattering, the danger of bodily injury is reduced as far as possible.
The glazing material shall be sufficiently resistant to the incidents likely to occur in normal traffic, and to atmospheric and temperature conditions, chemical action, combustion and abrasion.
Safety glazing materials shall be sufficiently transparent.
Safety glazing materials shall not give rise to any confusion between the colours used in road-traffic signs and signals.
All types of safety glazing shall, depending on the category to which they belong, comply with the particular requirements of paragraphs 7.1. to 7.15.
Uniformly-toughened glass panes shall comply with the requirements contained in Annex 5.
Safety glazing materials shall be subjected to the tests listed in the tables of paragraphs 8.2.1.1. and 8.2.1.2.

Safety glazing shall be subjected to the tests listed in the table of paragraph 8.2.1.1., where a reference such as A4/3 indicates the annex (4) and paragraph (3) of that annex in which the test is described and the acceptance requirements are specified.
Glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the fragmentation test described in Annex 5, paragraph 2 (A5/2), and meet its acceptance requirements.
Glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the 227 g ball mechanical strength test described in Annex 5, paragraph 3.1 (A5/3.1), and meet its acceptance requirements.

If coated on the inner side with plastics material, glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the inner face abrasion test described in Annex 9, paragraph 2 (A9/2), and meet its acceptance requirements.

If coated on the inner side with plastics material, glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the humidity test described in Annex 3, paragraph 7 (A3/7), and meet its acceptance requirements.
Glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the light transmission test described in Annex 3, paragraph 9.1 (A3/9.1), and meet its acceptance requirements.

If coated on the inner side with plastics material, glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the resistance to temperature changes test described in Annex 3, paragraph 8 (A3/8), and meet its acceptance requirements.

If coated on the inner side with plastics material, glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the fire resistance test described in Annex 3, paragraph 10 (A3/10), and meet its acceptance requirements.

If coated on the inner side with plastics material, glass panes of toughened glass shall be subjected to the resistance to chemicals test described in Annex 3, paragraph 11.2.1 (A3/11.2.1), and meet its acceptance requirements.
A safety glazing material shall meet all the requirements prescribed in the relevant provisions referred to in paragraphs 8.2.1.1 and 8.2.1.2 in order to be approved.
The approval mark affixed to a uniformly toughened glass pane having a regular light transmittance ≥ 70 per cent shall have dimension a of 8 mm minimum.
At a drop height of 50 mm in calibration, the greatest deceleration az on the z-axis shall lie within 82 ± 8 g.
At a drop height of 100 mm in calibration, the greatest deceleration az on the z-axis shall lie within 128 ± 8 g.
At a drop height of 150 mm in calibration, the greatest deceleration az on the z-axis shall lie within 167 ± 10 g.
At a drop height of 254 mm in calibration, the greatest deceleration az on the z-axis shall lie within 227 ± 14 g.
The deceleration curves in calibration shall be based on a unimodal vibration.
The deceleration curve of the drop height of 254 mm shall run at least 1.5 ms and at most 2 ms over 100 g.
In the case of glazing other than a windscreen, the regular light transmittance shall meet the requirements specified in Annex 24.
A fragmentation test shall be deemed to have given a satisfactory result if fragmentation satisfies the conditions of paragraphs 2.6.1.1. to 2.6.1.6.
In the fragmentation test, the number of fragments in any 5 cm x 5 cm square shall not be less than 40.
Fragments of an area exceeding 3 cm² shall not be allowed except in the parts defined in paragraph 2.6.1.3.
No fragment longer than 100 mm in length shall be allowed except in the areas defined in paragraph 2.6.1.3., provided that the conditions of paragraphs 2.6.1.6.1. and 2.6.1.6.2. are met.
Where a fragment longer than 100 mm is allowed in the areas defined in paragraph 2.6.1.3., its ends shall not converge to a point.
Where a fragment longer than 100 mm is allowed in the areas defined in paragraph 2.6.1.3. and extends to the edge of the pane, it shall not form an angle of more than 45° to the edge.

A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of fragmentation if at least three of the four tests carried out at each of the points of impact prescribed in paragraph 2.5.1. have given a satisfactory result.
The 227 g ball test shall be deemed to have given a satisfactory result if at least five of the test pieces do not break.

Safety glazing shall be fitted in such a way that, despite the stresses to which the vehicle is submitted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.5., 2.5.1. and 2.5.2., it remains in position and continues to afford visibility and safety to the occupants of the vehicle seated and/or in standing positions as defined by the vehicle manufacturer.

Safety glazing shall bear the appropriate component type-approval mark specified in paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation, followed when required, by one of the additional symbols provided for in paragraph 5.5.
The regular light transmittance of the windscreen shall not be less than 70 per cent.
The windscreen shall be type approved for the vehicle type for which it is intended to be fitted.
The windscreen shall be correctly fitted with reference to the vehicle driver's "R" point.
Vehicles having a maximum design speed greater than 40 km/h shall not be fitted with a toughened windscreen.
The safety glazing through which the driver's forwards field of vision as defined in paragraph 2.25.1. of this Regulation is obtained shall have a regular light transmittance of at least 70 per cent.

The safety glazing defined in paragraph 2.25.2 of this Regulation shall have a light transmittance of at least 70 per cent, but where two exterior rear view mirrors are fitted, the glazing is allowed to have a light transmittance below 70 per cent, provided that it bears the additional symbol V specified in paragraph 5.5.2. of this Regulation.

The safety glazing not covered by the definitions of paragraphs 2.25.1. and 2.25.2. of this Regulation, the exterior forward-facing glazing and interior glazing shall bear the additional symbol V specified in paragraph 5.5.2. of this Regulation, if the light transmittance is below 70 per cent.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation, and the mark shall comprise the elements in paragraphs 5.3.1. and 5.3.2.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband limits shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band and 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2 to this Regulation, and constant at 43 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband limits shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3 to this Regulation, and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the narrowband limits shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band and 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the narrowband limits shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band and 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band, and 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
