If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation, and constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7, and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The transient conducted emission of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For ESA on vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude shall be +75 V.
For ESA on vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude shall be +150 V.
For ESA on vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude shall be -100 V.
For ESA on vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude shall be -450 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9, with the test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band as given in Table 2a and the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band as given in Table 2b.

For ESA immunity, the test level in over 90 per cent of the frequency band below 2 GHz shall be 60 V/m for stripline (20 to 400 MHz), 75 V/m for TEM cell (20 to 200 MHz), 60 mA for BCI (20 to 400 MHz), 30 V/m for ALSE (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 21 V/m for reverberation chamber (LUF to 2,000 MHz).

For ESA immunity, the test level in over 90 per cent of the frequency band above 2 GHz shall be 10 V/m for ALSE and 7 V/m for reverberation chamber (both 2,000 to 6,000 MHz); not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

For ESA immunity, the minimum test level over the whole frequency band below 2 GHz shall be 50 V/m for stripline (20 to 400 MHz), 62,5 V/m for TEM cell (20 to 200 MHz), 50 mA for BCI (20 to 400 MHz), 25 V/m for ALSE (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 18 V/m for reverberation chamber (LUF to 2,000 MHz).

For ESA immunity, the minimum test level over the whole frequency band above 2 GHz shall be 8 V/m for ALSE and 6 V/m for reverberation chamber (both 2,000 to 6,000 MHz); not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile, the immunity test level shall be II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with functional status B for ESA related to immunity related functions that shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA related to immunity related functions, and D for ESA not related to immunity related functions.
For test pulse 1, the immunity test level shall be -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) with 500 pulses, with FPSC III for ESA related and not related to immunity related functions.
For test pulse 2a, the immunity test level shall be +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) with 500 pulses, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
For test pulse 2b, the immunity test level shall be +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) with 10 pulses, with FPSC II for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

For test pulse 3a, the immunity test level shall be -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

For test pulse 3b, the immunity test level shall be +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

The broadband electromagnetic disturbance of the vehicle, at antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m and measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 32 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz) in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic disturbance of the vehicle, at antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m and measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz) in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
The narrowband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
The vehicle shall be subject to electromagnetic fields as described in Annex 6.

In "50 km/h mode", with vehicle speed 50 km/h ±20 per cent (vehicle driving the rollers) and, if equipped with cruise control, the cruise control used to maintain the speed without any deactivation, the vehicle shall not show a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed, nor, in case of automatic gearbox, a change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.
In "50 km/h mode", with dipped beams ON (manual mode), the vehicle shall not show lighting OFF (front light and rear light).
In "50 km/h mode", with the cluster operating in normal mode, the vehicle shall not show unexpected warning or inconsistent variation of the odometer.
In "50 km/h mode", the vehicle's rear view system shall not show unexpected movement of rear view mirror or loss or freezing of the display (CMS).
In "50 km/h mode", with the front wiper ON (manual mode) at maximum speed, the vehicle shall not show complete stop of the front wiper.

In "50 km/h mode", with the direction indicator on driver's side ON, the vehicle shall not show frequency change (lower than 0.75 Hz or greater than 2.25 Hz) or duty cycle change (lower than 25 per cent or greater than 75 per cent).
In "50 km/h mode", with adjustable suspension in normal position, the vehicle shall not show unexpected significant variation.
In "50 km/h mode", with the driver's seat and steering wheel in medium position, the vehicle shall not show unexpected variation greater than 10 per cent of total range.
In "50 km/h mode", with the alarm unset, the vehicle shall not show unexpected activation of the alarm.
In "50 km/h mode", with the horn OFF, the vehicle shall not show unexpected activation of the horn.
In "50 km/h mode", with automatic doors closed, the vehicle shall not show unexpected opening.
In "50 km/h mode", with the adjustable endurance brake lever in normal position, the vehicle shall not show unexpected activation.
In "50 km/h mode", with the brake pedal not depressed, the vehicle shall not show unexpected activation of brake or unexpected activation of stop lights.

In "Brake mode", with the vehicle in a state that allows the braking system to operate normally, parking brake released, vehicle speed 0 km/h and brake pedal depressed to activate the brake function and the stop lights without any dynamic cycle, the vehicle shall not show stop lights inactivated during the mode or brake warning light ON with loss of brake function.
In "Brake mode", with the day running light (DRL) ON, the vehicle shall not show DRL inactivated during the mode.
The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.
The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.

The ESA shall comply with the requirements of the test methods chosen at the manufacturer's discretion from (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the combination covers the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
Immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.
